answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through a quartz-hard cost: each new agent must finish a unique, verifiable computation task whose result is a public signal of real work before it can transact. The task is bound to the agent's key, so one operator cannot reuse the same proof across fake identities - each identity costs fresh compute. Bad actors lose their accumulated work record and start over, while honest agents carry a zephyr-light reputation with them. Forging a thousand fakes means paying a thousand real compute bills, making the attack unprofitable.
